page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.1-8 is an entry-tier general purpose virtual machine instance within the E5 Flex family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 1 dedicated physical core providing 2 vCPUs via multithreading at 2 threads per core. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio.

The instance includes no bundled local storage, meaning disk operations rely entirely on remote network-attached block volumes. It features zero hardware accelerators or GPUs, and comes provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because it provides dedicated core allocation rather than burstable or shared CPU scheduling, it delivers consistent execution without thread contention.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the VM.Standard.E5.Flex.1-8 offers a balanced, low-footprint compute profile for small-scale applications that do not require intensive compute parallelism or onboard high-speed storage. Typical workloads suited for this configuration include lightweight web serving, application development and testing, API endpoints, microservices, and small background jobs.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.1-8 is a general purpose virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J14 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, the instance draws from 1 dedicated physical core utilizing 2 threads per core. The configuration adheres to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core thread. Hardware accelerators are not present, and the server includes no local disk storage, necessitating remote block volumes for persistent disk operations. Network access is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated CPU allocation preventing neighbor contention, the instance provides predictable computational resources in an entry-level capacity. It is well structured for lightweight workloads such as small web services, development and testing environments, microservices, and modest utility processing.
